question: What is the primary hormone secreted by the hypothalamus that starts the reproductive hormone chain?
explanation: The hypothalamus releases gonadotropin-releasing hormone to trigger the pituitary gland, which drives the entire reproductive hormone pathway. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h1)

question: Why is it clinically necessary to evaluate the male partner during infertility workups?

options.A: Women are rarely the sole cause of delayed conception
options.B: Male factors contribute to nearly half of all couple infertility cases
options.C: Government policies mandate joint fertility screenings
options.D: Male testing is much cheaper and faster than female testing

explanation: Because male issues are present in close to fifty percent of cases, evaluating both partners is essential for proper diagnosis. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h1)

question: How does the long-term use of external testosterone usually affect natural sperm production?

options.A: It directly stimulates the Sertoli cells to produce more mature sperm cells
options.B: It has no significant impact on the normal male reproductive system
options.C: It suppresses pituitary hormones via negative feedback and stops sperm production
options.D: It forces the hypothalamus to release higher amounts of GnRH

explanation: External androgens trick the brain into stopping natural hormone signals, which causes the testes to shut down sperm creation. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h2)

question: What defines a pre-testicular cause of male infertility?

options.A: A physical blockage within the epididymis preventing sperm release
options.B: A genetic mutation residing directly on the chromosomes inside the sperm
options.C: A hormonal or systemic problem outside the testes that disrupts sperm production
options.D: An infection of the prostate gland that damages the seminal fluid

explanation: Pre-testicular issues originate in the brain or endocrine system before the signal ever reaches the testicles. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h2)

question: What is the most common correctable physical cause of male infertility?
explanation: A varicocele is an enlarged set of veins in the scrotum that doctors can surgically repair to help restore normal fertility. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h3)

question: Why does an undescended testicle often lead to problems with future fertility?

options.A: The testicle fails to receive any blood supply throughout childhood and adolescence
options.B: Immune cells easily cross the blood-testis barrier and destroy the abnormal organ
options.C: The vas deferens naturally attaches to the wrong structure during development
options.D: Higher core body temperature inside the abdomen damages the delicate sperm-producing tissue

explanation: Testes need a cooler environment outside the main body cavity; staying inside the abdomen causes permanent heat damage. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h3)

question: What term describes the condition where semen flows backward into the urinary bladder during climax?
explanation: Retrograde ejaculation happens when the bladder neck fails to close properly, forcing semen backward instead of forward. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common post-testicular cause of male factor infertility?

options.A: Congenital absence of the vas deferens
options.C: Blockage of the vas deferens from previous surgery
options.D: Scarring of the epididymis from a chronic infection

explanation: A pituitary tumor is a pre-testicular hormonal issue, whereas post-testicular causes involve blockages or transport problems after sperm is made. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h4)

question: How does severe obesity negatively impact male reproductive health?

options.A: Obesity stops the pituitary gland from ever producing luteinizing hormone
options.B: Body fat physically blocks sperm from leaving the epididymis during ejaculation
options.C: Adipose cells directly attack mature sperm cells in the seminal fluid
options.D: Fat tissue converts extra testosterone into estrogen, disrupting the hormonal balance

explanation: Fatty tissue contains aromatase, an enzyme that turns testosterone into estrogen, which interferes with normal sperm creation. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h5)

question: A 32-year-old commercial bus driver presents with low sperm motility. Which lifestyle factor is most likely contributing to his condition?

options.A: Engaging in high-intensity cardiovascular endurance training
options.B: Prolonged daily sitting causing chronic scrotal heat elevation
options.C: Working in high-altitude environments for many hours
options.D: Consuming excessive amounts of dietary protein supplements

explanation: Professionals who sit for long hours often experience increased scrotal temperatures, which harms sperm quality. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h5)

question: What is the recommended period of sexual abstinence before providing a semen sample for analysis?
explanation: A standard abstinence window of two to seven days ensures reliable sperm count and quality measurements. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h6)

question: Why is a hormone profile including FSH, LH, and testosterone ordered during a male infertility workup?

options.A: To measure the exact temperature inside the scrotal sac
options.B: To check if pre-testicular endocrine imbalances are causing poor sperm production
options.C: To screen the patient for genetic chromosomal translocations
options.D: To confirm the presence of a physical blockage inside the vas deferens

explanation: Hormone blood tests show whether the brain and endocrine system are properly signaling the testicles to make sperm. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h6)

question: What assisted reproductive technique involves injecting a single sperm directly into an egg?
explanation: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) directly places one selected sperm into an egg to overcome severe male factor infertility. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h7)

question: Why is surgical repair of a varicocele performed in some infertile men?

options.A: To clear out bacterial infections located inside the prostate gland
options.B: To replace missing hormones normally produced by the pituitary gland
options.C: To lower scrotal temperature and improve overall sperm parameters
options.D: To bypass a physical blockage within the epididymis

explanation: Fixing a varicocele reduces excess heat and blood pooling around the testicle, often improving sperm count and movement. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h7)

question: How do cultural expectations in Nigeria often worsen the emotional strain of male infertility?

options.A: Society places heavy emphasis on fatherhood and family lineage, leading to deep personal stigma
options.B: Cultural practices strictly forbid men from undergoing any form of medical testing
options.C: Traditional healers are legally required to manage all reproductive health conditions
options.D: Communities automatically blame the female partner, protecting the man from stress

explanation: The strong cultural expectation to bear children creates intense psychological pressure and shame when fertility challenges arise. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h8)

question: A male patient appears quiet and defensive during his fertility workup. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Reassure him that male infertility is always easily cured with surgery
options.B: Provide a private, non-judgmental environment to discuss his concerns openly
options.C: Refer him immediately to a psychiatrist for severe clinical depression
options.D: Insist that his wife answers all the clinical questions for him

explanation: Creating a safe, supportive space helps lower defenses and encourages the patient to share his emotional burdens. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h8)
